raw_case_text:
A 20-year-old male came with complaints of multiple sinuses over the region of the scalp for a period of one year. He gave a similar history of sinus over the left eyelid since a year, with dystopia for the last six months. The dystopia was gradually progressive, painless, with no diminution of vision or diplopia [Fig. 1]. He further gave history of lacerated wound being sutured over the left eyebrow five years back, following fall on the left forehead.
On examination of the eyes, vision was 20/20 in both eyes. All findings in right eye were within normal limits. The left eye showed dystopia of 20 prism diopters (Delta) downwards and 10 Delta outwards on prism bar test. On exophthalmometry there was relative proptosis in left eye of 2 mm. The extraocular movements were within normal limits except for restriction in left gaze [Fig. 2]. The left eyelid showed a diffuse swelling with a discharging sinus. The anterior segment, pupil, fundus and diplopia charting were within normal limits. General examination showed multiple sinuses on the scalp which were draining white grains.
Apart from leucocytosis all routine investigations were within normal limits. Computer tomography (CT) scan of the brain revealed extradural invasion. CT of the orbit showed soft tissue swelling of the pre-septal area of the left upper eyelid with orbital involvement [Fig. 3]. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed increased left orbital volume and evident dystopia [Fig. 4].
Microbiology testing of the erosive scalp and lid lesions showed pus cells and Nocardia Asteroides / Nocardia Brazilensis bacillus, highly suggestive of actinomycetoma. Histopathology revealed lympho-histiocytic infiltration with focal abscess formation. Inset shows an eosinophilic granule exhibiting a Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon with a background of neutrophils [Fig. 5].
We started treatment with intravenous (IV) streptomycin 80 mg twice daily and tab. cotrimoxazole DS once daily for six weeks in intensive phase. Being a disease resistant to treatment, frequent change in antibiotics is desirable to avoid development of drug resistance. The patient was put on maintenance phase of tab. cotrimoxazole DS once daily and tab. rifampicin 600 mg once daily. He responded well to treatment with healing of sinuses and reduction in dystopia

subjective.chief_complaint: A 20-year-old male presented with a 1-year history of multiple draining sinuses over the scalp and left upper eyelid, accompanied by 6 months of progressive painless left ocular dystopia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient reported multiple sinuses discharging white grains over his scalp and a discharging sinus over his left upper eyelid for 1 year, followed by gradually progressive, painless downward and outward displacement (dystopia) of the left eye over the preceding 6 months without vision loss or diplopia.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of a sutured forehead/left eyebrow laceration following a fall 5 years prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for visual diminution, diplopia, or ocular pain.

objective.physical_examination: Visual acuity was 20/20 in both eyes; right eye exam was normal. The left eye exhibited diffuse upper eyelid swelling with a discharging sinus, downward dystopia of 20 prism diopters and outward dystopia of 10 prism diopters on prism bar testing, 2 mm of relative proptosis on exophthalmometry, and restricted levo-version (left gaze), with normal anterior segment, pupillary reflexes, fundus, and diplopia charting. General exam revealed multiple scalp sinuses draining white grains.
objective.routine_investigations: Routine blood tests were within normal limits except for leukocytosis.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT demonstrated extradural invasion, and orbital CT showed preseptal soft-tissue swelling of the left upper eyelid with intraorbital extension. Orbital MRI confirmed increased left orbital volume and marked globe dystopia. Histopathology of the lesion showed lymphohistiocytic infiltration with focal neutrophil-rich microabscesses containing eosinophilic granules with a Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Cranio-orbital actinomycetoma caused by Nocardia asteroides / Nocardia brasiliensis was confirmed by microbiological analysis of scalp and eyelid sinus discharge demonstrating pus cells and Nocardia asteroides / N. brasiliensis bacilli alongside characteristic histopathology. Intensive-phase therapy with IV streptomycin (80 mg twice daily) and oral double-strength cotrimoxazole (once daily) for 6 weeks followed by maintenance oral double-strength cotrimoxazole (once daily) plus oral rifampicin (600 mg once daily) led to complete healing of the scalp and eyelid sinuses and reduction of left ocular dystopia.
